what: a strix, the blood-drinking night bird of Roman legend described by Ovid, painted seriously as a sinister, starved predator: a great owl, a bird and nothing but a bird, but wrong. Its head is huge, round and as wide as its whole chest, with the flat round face of an owl: a broad disc of pale smoke-grey feathers framing both eyes, and both eyes side by side in the front of the face looking straight forward. The two eyes are enormous, round and staring, each a third of the face wide, bright lamp-yellow with a tiny black pupil, ringed with black. In the middle of the face, between and below the eyes, is a short, thick, sharply hooked beak of dark horn-grey, its tip wet with a little dark red blood. Its body is lean and scrawny under ragged feathers, dark smoke-grey and sooty black with pale dirty-white bars, the grey of wood ash and soot, never purple and never blue. Its two legs are feathered to the knee and end in long hooked black talons, the toes long and bony.
colours: ragged dark smoke-grey and sooty black feathers with pale dirty-white bars, a pale smoke-grey owl's face disc, bright lamp-yellow staring eyes with tiny black pupils ringed with black, a dark horn-grey hooked beak with a little dark red blood at its tip, long hooked black talons.
wears: It is a bird and wears nothing.
holds: It holds nothing: both taloned feet are empty, open and spread to snatch.
pose: Seen a little from the front, it swoops down toward the left with nothing beneath it, both broad ragged wings raised high above its back and bent sharply at the wrist like two tall arches, tips pointing down; its two legs are thrust forward together with the hooked talons spread wide to seize; its huge round head is turned to stare straight at the viewer, the hooked beak open.
must_show: an owl: a huge round flat owl's face, as wide as its chest, on a scrawny body
two enormous round staring yellow eyes side by side, facing forward
a short thick hooked beak with a little blood at the tip
ragged smoke-grey and sooty black feathers, no purple
two legs with long hooked talons thrust forward, swooping

what: a greater Erinyes, one of the three Furies of Greek tragedy as Aeschylus showed them, the old terrible goddesses who hunt murderers: a tall, lean, terrible woman with realistic adult proportions, a small head, long limbs, about eight heads tall, two arms, standing on two legs. Her skin is cold ash-grey, the grey of a stone statue, on her face, neck, arms and hands alike, a colour no living woman has. Her face is gaunt and furious, with hollow cheeks, a hooked nose, thin black lips drawn back from white teeth, and two wide staring eyes that are solid black; from each eye a thick bright streak of strong red blood, as wide as her finger, runs straight down her grey cheek to her chin, the brightest colour in the picture. She has no hair: growing from her scalp in its place are six thick living black snakes with pale yellow bellies, each as thick as her wrist, rearing out round her head with their mouths open. Two more black snakes are wound round her forearms like bracelets, their heads hissing at her wrists. From her back grow two great ragged wings of dark grey-black vulture feathers.
colours: cold ash-grey skin, solid black eyes with two thick bright streaks of strong red blood running down the cheeks, thick black snakes with pale yellow bellies in place of hair and round her forearms, ragged dark grey-black vulture-feather wings, a long black wool robe with a dull bronze border at the hem, a dull bronze belt.
wears: She wears a long black wool robe with long sleeves and a high neck that covers her from the throat to the ankles, its hem torn into ragged points above a dull bronze border, and a dull bronze belt. Her feet are bare. No armour, no crown, no jewels.
holds: In her right fist she holds exactly one scourge of snakes: the tails of three live black snakes gripped together in her fist like the lashes of a whip, each snake as thick as her thumb and as long as her arm, all three swinging out in one long curve over her head with their heads at the far end, mouths open. Her left hand is empty: a bare grey clawed hand, fingers spread, thrust forward. Nothing else is in her hands. She has no staff and no stick.
pose: On two legs, seen a little from the front, she rushes forward to the left with her weight on her bent front leg and her back leg stretched out behind, her body leaning far in and twisted, her right arm swung high back over her head lashing the scourge of snakes forward in a long curve, her empty clawed left hand thrust out ahead at the viewer, both wings raised high behind her and bent sharply at the wrist like two tall arches, tips pointing down, her robe whipping back; her bleeding black eyes stare straight at the viewer, her mouth open in a scream.
must_show: a gaunt grey-skinned woman with thick black snakes in place of hair
solid black eyes with streaks of blood running down the cheeks
black snakes wound round her forearms
two great ragged dark vulture-feather wings
a long black robe, fully clothed, no armour
a scourge of three snakes swung from the right fist; the left hand empty
rushing and lashing: a violent pose, not standing straight

what: a Ker, one of the Keres, the Greek death-spirits Hesiod painted on the shield of Heracles, who fight over the fallen to drink their blood, painted seriously as a terrible daimon: a lean, wiry, fully fleshed female spirit with realistic adult proportions, a small head, long limbs, about eight heads tall, two arms, two legs. Her skin is dark ash-grey, the grey of cold soot, with no blue in it, on her face, neck, arms and hands alike, a colour no living woman has. She is never pretty: her face is a monster's, long and gaunt, with hollow cheeks, a hooked nose, pointed ears, two small eyes of solid pale yellow light under a heavy brow, and a huge mouth stretched open from ear to ear, the lips drawn back from two rows of long pointed fangs, big and bright white, gnashing, the brightest thing in her face. Long wild ragged hair of dirty grey-white streams back from her head. Her long bony fingers end in long hooked claws of pale bone, as long as the fingers, with a little dark red blood on the points. From her back grow two leathery bat-like wings of dark charcoal-grey skin.
colours: dark ash-grey skin like cold soot, solid pale yellow eyes, big bright white fangs, long wild dirty grey-white hair, dark charcoal-grey leathery wings, a torn cloak and long dress of strong dark blood-red cloth, long hooked claws of pale bone with a little dark red blood on the points.
wears: She wears a long sleeveless dress of strong dark blood-red cloth that covers her from the throat to the shins, and over her shoulders a long cloak of the same blood-red cloth, torn into long ragged strips that stream and flap out behind her. A plain dark leather belt. Her arms and feet are bare. No armour, no crown, no jewels.
holds: Her hands are empty and she holds nothing: both clawed hands are open and reaching, the long hooked claws spread to seize.
pose: She dives down toward the left out of the air with nothing beneath her, her body stretched out and leaning steeply forward, both clawed arms thrust out ahead to seize, her legs trailing behind, both leathery wings raised high and bent sharply at the wrist like two tall arches, the ragged blood-red cloak streaming back; her face is turned toward the viewer, mouth wide open baring the white teeth.

big bright white gnashing fangs in a huge open mouth

what: Stheno the Gorgon, the mighty, immortal elder sister of Medusa, the fierce fighter of the two: a tall, powerful, terrible winged woman-shaped monster standing on two legs, nothing like a living lady, with realistic adult proportions, a small head, long limbs, about eight heads tall, with two arms only and no more. Her skin is cold ash-grey, the plain neutral grey of a weathered stone statue, on her face, neck and upper arms alike, a colour no living woman has. Her face is the gorgon mask from an old Greek shield: broad and fierce, with a heavy scowling brow, a flat wide nose, two huge round glaring eyes filled to the brim with solid yellow light, and a very wide mouth stretched open in a snarl from cheek to cheek, showing a row of teeth and two long white tusks curving up from the lower jaw. She has no hair: growing from her whole scalp in its place are seven very thick living snakes, each as thick as her arm, glossy black with pale yellow bellies, rearing up and outward with their white mouths gaping. Her hands and forearms, from the elbow down, are solid bright bronze metal, polished and gleaming, and each bronze finger ends in a long hooked bronze claw. From her back grow two great wings of feathers of dull dark old gold, the dun brown-gold of tarnished brass, darker brown at the tips, never bright.
colours: cold ash-grey skin, huge solid glowing yellow eyes, white tusks, seven thick glossy black snakes with pale yellow bellies, bright polished bronze hands and forearms with bronze claws, two great wings of dull dark old gold feathers, dun brown-gold like tarnished brass, a long dark charcoal-black peplos, a corselet of dark bronze scales, a broad bronze belt.
wears: She wears a long archaic Greek peplos of dark charcoal-black wool that covers her from the shoulders to the ankles; its skirt is heavy, thick, opaque wool, whole and closed all the way round from the waist to the ankles, a single unbroken bell of cloth that hides both legs completely, nothing showing through it; over it, from her collar to her hips, a heavy corselet of small overlapping dark bronze scales, straight-sided and flat across the chest like a soldier's, no cups and no discs, and a broad bronze belt. No crown, no diadem, no jewels.
holds: Her hands are empty and she holds nothing: two bronze hands with long hooked bronze claws, fingers spread to strike.
pose: On two legs under the peplos, seen from the side and a little from the front, she lunges forward to the left to attack, her body pitched far forward, her weight on her bent front leg, body twisted, her right bronze hand raised high above her head with the claws spread to rake down, her left bronze hand thrust forward low with the claws spread, her tusked mouth wide open, her yellow eyes glaring straight at the viewer, every snake of her hair rearing and striking, both golden wings spread high behind her and bent sharply at the wrist like two tall arches, tips pointing down.

seven very thick black snakes for hair, readable in the small sprite

what: Euryale the Gorgon, the far-roaming, immortal sister of Medusa, the wailer who still grieves for her beheaded sister: a tall, terrible winged woman-shaped monster standing on two legs, nothing like a living lady, with realistic adult proportions, a small head, long limbs, about eight heads tall, with two arms only and no more. Her skin is cold ash-grey, the plain neutral grey of a weathered stone statue, on her face, neck and upper arms alike, a colour no living woman has. Her face is never a human woman's face: it is the gorgon mask from an old Greek shield, broad and round and monstrous, with a heavy brow, a flat wide nose, two huge round eyes filled to the brim with solid yellow light, and a very wide mouth stretched open from cheek to cheek as far as it will go in a howl of grief, showing a row of teeth and two long white tusks curving up from the lower jaw. She has no hair: growing from her whole scalp in its place are seven very thick living snakes, each as thick as her arm, glossy black with pale yellow bellies, writhing up and outward with their white mouths open, keening with her. Her hands and forearms, from the elbow down, are solid bright bronze metal, polished and gleaming, and each bronze finger ends in a long hooked bronze claw. From her back grow two great wings of feathers of dull dark old gold, the dun brown-gold of tarnished brass, darker brown at the tips, never bright.
colours: cold ash-grey skin, huge solid glowing yellow eyes, white tusks, seven thick glossy black snakes with pale yellow bellies, bright polished bronze hands and forearms with bronze claws, two great wings of dull dark old gold feathers, dun brown-gold like tarnished brass, a long mourning peplos of dark brown, the brown of a chestnut, with a broad black border, a black wool shawl.

what: an heir of Autolycus, the master thief of Greek myth and grandfather of Odysseus, to whom the god Hermes gave the gift of stealing: a lean, quick, wiry grown man of about thirty-five with realistic adult proportions, a small head, long limbs, about eight heads tall. He has weather-beaten light tan skin, a narrow clever face with a sharp nose, a short black beard trimmed close, and a sly sideways grin, his dark eyes glancing back at the viewer.
colours: weather-beaten light tan skin, a short black beard, a broad-brimmed traveller's hat of dark brown felt, a short tunic of undyed off-white linen, a short travelling cloak of dark charcoal-grey wool pinned at the right shoulder with a bronze pin, a dark brown leather belt, laced dark brown leather sandals, a short knife with a bright steel blade, a fat round pouch of dark brown leather with a few gold coins.
wears: He wears an ancient Greek traveller's outfit: a broad-brimmed round petasos hat of dark brown felt on his head with a cord under the chin, a short belted tunic of undyed off-white linen to mid-thigh, a short dark charcoal-grey wool travelling cloak pinned at the right shoulder and flying out behind him, a dark brown leather belt, and dark brown sandals laced up the shins. No armour, no hood, no mask.
holds: In his right hand he holds exactly one short knife no longer than his hand, with a bright steel blade and a dark wooden grip, held low and forward. In his left hand, held up and out to the side, he holds exactly one fat round drawstring purse of dark brown leather, the size of his fist, a few gold coins spilling from its mouth. Nothing else is in his hands.

what: a medium of Endor, of the line of the woman the Bible tells of, who called up the dead prophet Samuel for King Saul: an old woman necromancer of the ancient Near East, painted seriously like a figure from an old Bible illustration, grim, cold and uncanny, never a kindly grandmother and never a storybook witch. She is a gaunt, stooped, bony old woman of about seventy with realistic adult proportions, a small head, long limbs, about eight heads tall, two arms. She has weather-beaten light tan skin, deeply lined and drawn tight over the bones, a long hooked nose, sunken cheeks, thin lips pulled back in a grim whisper, and two blind-looking milky white eyes with no pupils, staring; her long grey hair hangs from under her headscarf. Her long bony fingers end in long dirty nails.
colours: weather-beaten light tan wrinkled skin, long grey hair, milky white eyes with no pupils, a long layered robe of very dark brown wool, nearly black, the colour of wet peat, an outer mantle of black wool with a fringed edge, a long headscarf of dark indigo wool, a headband of small dull bronze coins, a short knife with a pale carved bone blade, a thick curling column of pale grey-white ghost-smoke.
wears: She wears the layered dress of an old woman of ancient Israel: a long ankle-length robe of very dark brown wool, nearly black, the colour of wet peat, and over it a long black wool mantle with a knotted fringe at its edge, wrapped round her shoulders; a long headscarf of dark indigo wool covers her head and falls down her back, with a band of small dull bronze coins across her forehead. Her feet are in plain dark sandals. No pointed hat, no hood, no jewels besides the coins.
holds: In her right hand, drawn back by her hip, she holds exactly one short knife no longer than her hand, its blade of pale carved bone, its grip wrapped in dark cord. Her left hand is thrust up and forward, a bare open palm turned upward, and out of the whole palm rises one thick curling column of pale grey-white ghost-smoke, as thick as her wrist and as tall as her head, joined to the hand and rising from it, nothing else in the hand or near it. She holds no cigarette, no pipe, no candle and no staff.
pose: On two legs, seen from the side and a little from the front, she lunges forward to the left, bent far over, her weight on her bent front leg, her left arm thrust up and forward with the column of ghost-smoke pouring up out of the open palm, her right hand holding the bone knife drawn back by her hip ready to stab, her blind white eyes glaring at the viewer, her mouth open in a hissing incantation, her mantle and headscarf swinging back.

a band of small bronze coins across her forehead

one short pale bone knife in the right hand

what: a handmaid of Hel, the Norse goddess of the dead, one of the slow-walkers who serve in her hall: a dead woman who walks again, painted seriously like a figure from a Norse saga, uncanny and cold. She is a corpse: a tall, thin, stooped dead woman with realistic adult proportions, a small head, long limbs, about eight heads tall, two arms. Her face is the face of a woman three days dead: cold chalk-white dead skin with a grey-blue tinge, deep hollow cheeks, a thin pinched nose, ears, heavy half-closed eyelids, thin blue-grey lips dried back from her teeth, the mouth hanging slack and open, and two sunken blank white eyes with no pupils, dark grey-black rings round them like bruises. Like her mistress Hel she is half dead-dark: both her bare hands and forearms, from the elbow down, are rotting and blackened, very dark slate-grey mottled with black, the skin shrunk and cracked over the bones so every knuckle, tendon and finger bone shows, the long thin fingers ending in long broken dark nails, plainly bare dead flesh, never gloves; the darkness creeps up past her elbows in uneven blotches. Long straight lank grey-white hair hangs loose to her waist.
colours: cold chalk-white dead skin on the face and neck, rotting blackened very dark slate-grey hands and forearms mottled with black, sunken blank white eyes, long lank grey-white hair, a long plain dress of dull slate blue-grey wool, the colour of a rain cloud, an apron of undyed off-white linen, two oval bronze brooches, a string of amber beads, a long-handled ladle of dark old wood, two big shiny domed bronze brooches.
wears: She wears the dress of a Norse woman: a long plain dress of dull slate blue-grey wool with long sleeves pushed up to the elbow, covering her from the neck to the ankles, and over it a long apron of undyed off-white linen hung from two shoulder straps; where each strap meets the apron, high on her chest below each collarbone, is pinned one big oval brooch of shiny bronze, each as big as her palm and domed like a turtle shell, the two brooches the brightest metal in the picture, with a short string of dull amber beads hanging between them. Her feet are bare. No crown, no hood, no armour.
holds: In her right hand, held low at her side, she holds exactly one wooden ladle: one straight thin stick of dark old wood as long as her forearm, with one small round cup at its lower end, empty; no basket, no pan, no bucket. Her left hand is thrust forward, a bare blackened rotting hand with the bony fingers spread and clawing, empty, nothing in it or near it. She has no staff.
pose: On two legs, seen from the side and a little from the front, she lurches forward to the left in a long dragging stride, stooped far over, her weight on her bent front leg, her back foot dragging behind on its toes, her head thrust forward and hanging, her jaw slack, her blank white eyes staring at the viewer, her blackened left arm reaching straight out at the level of her shoulder toward the viewer to touch, the ladle hanging in her right hand, her long grey hair swinging forward.

rotting blackened bare hands and forearms, plainly flesh, not gloves
a long slate blue-grey Norse dress with an off-white apron and two big shiny oval bronze brooches on the chest, fully clothed
one wooden ladle in the right hand

what: a mere-wife, one of the kind of Grendel's mother from the Old English poem Beowulf, the monstrous she-troll who lives under the black water of a mere: a huge, hunched, immensely powerful monster woman standing on two legs, painted seriously and frighteningly, never pretty, never a mermaid. She is a she-troll, alive and fully fleshed, heavy and big-boned like a she-bear: a thick heavy body, broad round shoulders, long heavy arms reaching nearly to her knees with big hands, a stooped hunched back, a small head sunk forward on a thick neck, thick legs with big clawed webbed feet; she is heavy and strong, never skinny and never a sculpted muscle-woman. Her skin is wet, slimy and glistening, very dark murky grey-green, the dull colour of a pike's back, mottled with black blotches, a colour no living person has, never bright green, on her face, neck, arms, hands and feet alike, with rough scaly patches on her shoulders and forearms. Her face is a living troll-woman's face, never a skull and never an ape's: long and haggard, with a long hooked nose, long pointed ears, sunken cheeks, a wide thin-lipped mouth full of jagged yellow-white fangs, and two small round eyes glowing pale lamp-yellow. Long lank wet black hair hangs over her shoulders in dripping strands. Her fingers end in long hooked black claws.

Her arms and feet are bare. No armour, no jewels.

Her left hand is empty: a huge green clawed hand stretched forward, fingers spread, reaching to grab and drag. Nothing else is in her hands.
pose: On two legs, seen from the side and a little from the front, she lunges forward to the left out of the dark, body pitched far forward and hunched low, her weight on her bent front leg, her back leg stretched out behind, her empty clawed left hand thrust out far ahead at the viewer to grab, her right arm raised high above her head holding the broad seax up against the backdrop, clear of her body, point forward, ready to stab down, her fanged mouth open in a snarl, wet hair swinging, water dripping from her arms.

what: a gashadokuro, the starving giant skeleton of Japanese folk tales, built from the bones of the unburied dead: an enormous skeleton and nothing else, with no muscle, no flesh and no skin on it anywhere, so big that it fills the whole picture from edge to edge. It is built nothing like a man's slim skeleton: it is hunched and enormously broad, nearly as wide as it is tall, every bone three times as thick as a man's. Its skull is huge and heavy, set low and thrust forward on a thick arched spine, with two deep black eye sockets, in each one round spot of solid bright red light as big as its nose, and its long jaw hangs wide open to bite, showing big blunt teeth; inside the open mouth is only empty pitch-black darkness, no tongue. Its ribcage is broad and deep, made of six very thick ribs with wide black gaps between them. Its arm bones are as thick as posts, thicker than its legs, ending in huge bony hands with long finger bones. All of the bone is old, chalk grey-white with dark grey cracks, on the skull, ribs, arms and legs alike, never gold and never yellow. Its finger bones are long and end in hooked points like claws.

wears: It wears nothing at all: bare bones only. No armour, no helmet, no cloth.
holds: Both hands are empty and it holds nothing: two huge bony hands thrust forward, the long hooked finger bones spread wide like claws to grab. It has exactly two arms and two hands.

what: the Hellmouth of medieval church Doom paintings and mystery plays: the colossal gaping head of Leviathan, the great beast of the Book of Job, and nothing but the head. It is seen from the front and a little from the side, its jaws flung open as wide as they will go, the open mouth taking up more than half the picture. It is a monstrous beast's head, part whale, part dragon: a heavy blunt snout on top with two flared smoking nostrils, small deep-set eyes glowing fierce amber-yellow under heavy horny brows, two short thick curved horns of dark horn, and rows of big scales. The upper jaw is lifted high and the lower jaw dropped low, both lined with rows of huge curved fangs, each as long as a man's arm, dull yellowed ivory-white. Deep inside the open throat a furnace of fire burns, bright orange and yellow flames rising from the dark gullet, the lips and jaws around it nearly black. Behind the jaws the head ends in a ragged ruff of scaled hide and spikes; there is no neck and no body.

pose: The great head lunges forward and to the left, tilted, the jaws flung open wider than any animal's, the upper jaw thrown up and the lower jaw thrust down toward the viewer, the fire in its throat flaring up out of the gullet, two short wisps of smoke from its nostrils joined to the snout.

what: the crawling blood of Tiamat, the salt sea goddess of the Babylonian creation poem, cut from her body by Marduk: a shapeless heaving mass of thick dark sea-blood and brine, painted seriously with real weight and substance, never a cartoon slime. It is one rounded mound of thick liquid, longer than it is tall, soft all over, heaving and surging forward, lopsided, with smooth unbroken glossy wet skin, no streaks and no grain, its whole surface the same dark blood: crimson so deep it is nearly black in the hollows, the strong red of red sealing wax on the bulging curves where the light catches it, with bright wet highlights. Its lower edge is rounded and tucked under like a drop of thick liquid; it does not spread out flat. From its body four thick tendrils of the same dark blood lash out, each as thick as a quarter of the mass at its root and tapering evenly to a sharp point, curved like a sabre blade: one swept up and to the left, one swept up and to the right, one thrust forward low to the left, one swept back to the right. The mass itself has no eyes and no features; instead there is one big round staring eye, pale cold yellow with a black slit pupil, set partway along each of three of the tendrils, each eye as wide as its tendril.
colours: a thick glossy mass of crimson so dark it is nearly black in the hollows, the strong red of red sealing wax on the lit ridges, tapering tendrils of the same dark crimson, pale cold yellow eyes with black slit pupils.
pose: The whole mass surges forward to the left, heaving and lopsided, its four tapering tendrils lashing out in their four directions, the eyes on the tendrils staring at the viewer. Nothing is around or beneath it: its lower edge is the same dark glossy blood as the rest, with clear backdrop under it.
must_show: a shapeless heaving mass of dark crimson-black blood, not purple
four thick lashing tendrils that taper to sharp points, with no heads
a few big staring yellow eyes on the tendrils, never arranged as a face
surging forward, wet and heavy, painted, not a cartoon blob
clear backdrop under and around it
must_not_show: one big head on top of the mass
